title: Personal Project (Assessment 5)
summary: Assessment 5: build your own full-stack app. Kickoff is Fri Dec 4 (Judith's Workshop), the deadline is Tue Dec 22 and presentations are Wed Dec 23, with project work time on most afternoons in between. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Plan, build, document and present a complete full-stack app of your own.
required: Build a full-stack app (syllabus: Assessment 5, Personal Project). Deadline Dec 22; presentations Dec 23.

React + Vite front end with multiple components and pages, client-side routing, forms for creating and updating data, and calls to your Django API (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)
Django API back end: models, serializers, views, URLs, authentication and database-backed resources (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)
A docker-compose.yml that runs the React front end, Django back end, database and Nginx, so someone can clone and run it (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)
User authentication: register, log in, log out, and protected features only when logged in (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)
At least 3 full CRUD resources, each with its own model and a real role in the app (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)
At least 1 third-party API that fits the app's purpose (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)
At least 1 LLM feature tied to the app's purpose (they recommended Gemini) (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)
A polished, intentional front-end design: clear layout, navigation, consistent styling, helpful feedback (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)

A detailed README.md: description, tech stack, features, install steps, environment variables, Docker, API info, the third-party API, the LLM feature, known issues and future improvements (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)
Deployment is ideal but not required (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)

A recorded video walkthrough submitted through a Launch Point form. This cohort has live presentations on Dec 23, so confirm which applies (per a previous cohort's guidelines; confirm with instructors)

steps.title: Pick your idea before kickoff
steps.detail: Choose something you'd actually use, so you'll stay motivated for three weeks. Check it naturally fits auth, 3 CRUD resources, a third-party API and an LLM feature. You don't have an "own app" yet, and the instructors put your own app first in homework priority, so starting it early helps everywhere.
steps.doneWhen: You have a one-paragraph pitch: what the app does, who it's for and what problem it solves.

steps.title: Stress-test the plan with /grill-me
steps.detail: Let Claude question your idea until the vague parts are gone. Answer the questions yourself; that's where the learning is.
steps.code: /grill-me I'm planning my Code Platoon personal project (React + Vite, Django, Postgres, Docker Compose). Here's my pitch: <YOUR PITCH>. Grill me on scope, my 3 CRUD resources, the third-party API and the LLM feature until the plan is clear.
steps.doneWhen: You've answered the grilling and written down your decisions (scope, the 3 resources, the API, the LLM feature).

steps.title: Write the planning files
steps.detail: Create app_outline/, user_stories.md and api_notes.md in the new project (Netflix is still missing these, so this is good practice). List each CRUD resource with its fields, the user stories, and the endpoints you'll need.
steps.doneWhen: All three planning files exist and name the 3 resources, the third-party API and the LLM feature.

steps.title: Set up the repo and skeleton
steps.detail: Make a new repo under cruzjay188 using the curriculum's client/ + server/ + db/ layout. Add .env to .gitignore before the first commit. FS 1 (Dec 3) teaches the Compose setup you'll use here.
steps.doneWhen: `docker compose up` starts the database, Django and React on your Mac, and `git check-ignore .env` prints `.env`.

concepts.meaning: Minimum viable product: the smallest version that does the core job. Build it first, polish later.
A one-line need: "As a <user>, I want <goal> so that <reason>."
One kind of data users can create, read, update and delete, like recipes.
A feature that sends your app's data to an AI model and uses the answer.
